newsitem.title: JAPAN: Top Japan health bureaucrat resigns over scandal.
newsitem.headline: Top Japan health bureaucrat resigns over scandal.

text.p: The top bureaucrat in Japan's troubled Health and Welfare Ministry resigned on Tuesday over a money scandal, Health Minister Junichiro Koizumi said.

Koizumi told a news conference he accepted Vice Minister Nobuharu Okamitsu's resignation after reports said he took a golf club membership worth 13 million yen ($117,000) from the owner of a private chain of welfare institutions that provided care for ill elderly people.

In a news conference on Monday, Okamitsu, 57, denied receiving free use of the golf club membership but hours later newspapers reported club records showed Okamitsu played golf at the club using the membership.
Golf memberships are highly prized and considered assets in Japan where a membership can cost more than 11 million yen ($99,000) a year.
Okamitsu has admitted using a luxury car provided by the owner of the welfare institutions, Hiroshi Koyama, who was arrested last week on unrelated bribery charges.

The Health and Welfare Ministry has already been under fire this year, accused of negligence over tainted blood products which led to AIDS and incompetence over a deadly food poisoning outbreak. ($1=111 yen)
